acceptanceCriteria: After a core binary update that changes the index engine key, the next SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hook in an already-indexed checkout does not degrade with dogfood-event-index-snapshot-stale; either the updater rebuilt the snapshot for live heads, or the hook started one bounded background refresh and said so.

Any automatic refresh writes only derived state under the Git common dir's corvint/index store, honours the existing eviction bound, never runs inside a read command's own path, and records its outcome (built, skipped, failed) visibly.
A regression test covers update-then-hook on a fixture repository; the governing spec records the requirement, non-goals (no permanent daemon), failure modes and rollback.
body: Observed 2026-10-09 on darwin-arm64 in /Users/russelllewis/projects/corvint. At 21:42 the installed corvint was replaced by Corvint 1.0.0-rc.2 (build 404) (engine key cd22c042fc84a53e) from build 360 (engine a7293de93d52e9e6). A snapshot already existed for the main checkout's HEAD tree 0cb16f6e0edeb09b390768f14102e11085419a65 under the old engine (sha1-0cb16f6e...-a7293de93d52e9e6.gob), but snapshots are keyed by engine, so every subsequent Claude Code SessionStart (including source=compact) and UserPromptSubmit hook degraded: 'Corvint FALLBACK degraded: corvint-event-rejected:dogfood-event-index-snapshot-stale ... Refresh the snapshot once, outside the hook: corvint --root ... index --if-stale'. The user saw this after a compaction and asked why and whether it could happen automatically. Running the suggested command took 2.0 s wall (6359 sources) and cleared it. Expected: a binary update does not leave every session degraded until a manual reindex. Candidate designs: (a) corvint-update apply --component core rebuilds snapshots for live heads (it is already an explicit operator mutation); (b) the SessionStart hook, on a stale snapshot, launches one detached, bounded 'index --if-stale' and reports it, without blocking the hook deadline; (c) reuse an old-engine snapshot when the engine change does not alter the snapshot encoding. Invariant 4 (read commands do not mutate) and 7 (no permanent daemon) constrain (b).
title: Index snapshot goes stale for every session after a core binary update until a manual corvint index --if-stale
